title: Architecture assessment: supervision second pass — wire detection plane + loop detector + timeout classification + alert evidence
summary: Architectural assessment of the task_planner's plan (commit 6092b5a7a, v1) for issue #3665. Verdict: ACK. All technical claims verified against the live tree at main @ 1cd0c8ad7. The plan correctly identifies four areas of work (signals not consulted, session boundaries as failures, undetectable loops, unactionable alerts) decomposed into 5 linear slices (snapshot population → detection plane wiring → loop detector → timeout classification → alert evidence). The detection plane (#2270) is fully built but completely unwired: snapshot_from_health_context() populates only 5 of 13 EventStreamSnapshot fields, and _run_overseer_detection_plane() has zero call sites. The timeout classification bug is confirmed: _classify_exit() treats exit code -1 as FAILED, consuming retry budget. The loop detector is absent — no detect_tool_input_loop() exists, midturn_messages is never populated. The convergence-stall false positive is confirmed: both _check_convergence_stall() and _has_recent_peer_progress() use get_latest_progress_timestamp() but with different gate windows. The linear slice structure is correct (shared files per #3046). Four non-blocking architectural refinements are noted: (1) double-evaluation guard should be per-pipeline not global lock; (2) midturn_messages population depends on truncated log parsing — consider BRC tracker records; (3) timeout detection via error message is fragile — consider pod active_deadline_seconds; (4) timestamp source is already unified — fix should unify the gate window, not the source. Scope is correctly limited to Tier 1+2 items from the 30-item candidate list.

risks: slice-2 TASK-2-1 (hot-loop wiring): double-evaluation guard must be per-pipeline, not a global lock, to avoid cross-pipeline contention
slice-2 TASK-2-1: detection plane must be exception-isolated — must not crash the runtime tick loop
slice-4 TASK-4-3: timeout classification must distinguish exit -1 from asyncio.timeout vs exit -1 from other failures via error message
slice-3 TASK-3-1: loop detector must be deterministic (no LLM) and handle variable cycle shapes (1-, 2-, 3-, 8-cycles)
slice-1 TASK-1-5: midturn_messages population depends on log parsing fidelity (truncated at ~100 chars)
non_goals: Rebuilding the overseer agent (working; problem is input pipeline)
Removing the HealthMonitor tripwires (wired and working)
Adding LLM classification to the hot path (expensive Haiku calls)
Changing the 2-hour timeout default (7200s is reasonable)
Tier 3-5 from the candidate list (input to the gate, not a work queue)

slice_dag.rationale: Slices share overlapping files (kubernetes_monitor.py, detection_plane.py, health_monitor.py) so they must be a linear chain per #3046. The plan's ordering is correct: snapshot population first (prerequisite for all detectors), then detection plane wiring (enables loop detector and alert routing), then loop detector (depends on midturn_messages), then timeout classification (shares kubernetes_monitor.py), then alert evidence (depends on detection plane findings).
